questions.stem: This H&E section of cardiac muscle shows a dense interstitial infiltrate of small mononuclear cells with adjacent myocyte damage. What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: An interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate with associated myocyte injury defines lymphocytic myocarditis, a common cause of secondary dilated cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: An interstitial lymphocytic infiltrate with associated myocyte injury defines lymphocytic myocarditis, a common cause of secondary dilated cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: On this labeled frontal chest radiograph, the cardiac silhouette occupies more than half the thoracic width. What abnormality does this represent?

explanation.summary: A cardiothoracic ratio greater than 0.5 on a PA film defines cardiomegaly, a common radiographic finding in dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: A cardiothoracic ratio greater than 0.5 on a PA film defines cardiomegaly, a common radiographic finding in dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

questions.stem: Compared with the normal heart shown alongside, the diseased heart has a globally enlarged, thin-walled chamber. What functional consequence best characterizes this disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impaired diastolic filling with preserved ejection fraction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduced systolic contractile function (low ejection fraction)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restriction of ventricular filling by rigid walls

choices.label: E
choices.text: Isolated valvular regurgitation with normal myocardium

explanation.summary: Dilated cardiomyopathy causes eccentric remodeling with chamber enlargement and wall thinning, impairing contractility and producing systolic (reduced ejection fraction) heart failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dilated cardiomyopathy causes eccentric remodeling with chamber enlargement and wall thinning, impairing contractility and producing systolic (reduced ejection fraction) heart failure.

questions.stem: Relative to the normal heart, the diseased heart in this diagram shows enlargement of which chambers?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right atrium and right ventricle only

choices.label: C
choices.text: The atria only, with normal ventricles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Left atrium and left ventricle only

choices.label: E
choices.text: The ventricles only, with thickened walls

explanation.summary: Dilated cardiomyopathy characteristically dilates all four chambers with wall thinning, distinguishing it from the isolated or concentric changes seen in other cardiomyopathies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dilated cardiomyopathy characteristically dilates all four chambers with wall thinning, distinguishing it from the isolated or concentric changes seen in other cardiomyopathies.

questions.stem: This gross heart specimen, cut open beside a ruler, shows a markedly dilated ventricular cavity with a thinned, flabby wall and prominent trabeculae. What is the diagnosis?

explanation.summary: A dilated, thin-walled ventricular chamber with an increased volume-to-mass ratio is the classic gross appearance of dilated cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: A dilated, thin-walled ventricular chamber with an increased volume-to-mass ratio is the classic gross appearance of dilated cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: When sarcomeres are added in series as depicted (bottom row) rather than in parallel, what change in ventricular geometry results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wall thickening with a narrowed chamber

explanation.summary: Volume overload drives sarcomere addition in series, lengthening myocytes and dilating the ventricular cavity, the cellular basis of eccentric hypertrophy seen in dilated cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Volume overload drives sarcomere addition in series, lengthening myocytes and dilating the ventricular cavity, the cellular basis of eccentric hypertrophy seen in dilated cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: This gross cross-section of a heart shows marked, uniform thickening of the left ventricular free wall and interventricular septum with a small, slit-like chamber. This pattern of remodeling most commonly develops in response to which hemodynamic stress?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A high-output state such as chronic anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infiltration of the myocardium by amyloid protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Chronic volume overload from mitral regurgitation

explanation.summary: Uniform, concentric thickening of the LV wall with a reduced cavity size is the hallmark of concentric hypertrophy, which arises when the ventricle must generate sustained high pressures against an increased afterload (hypertension, aortic stenosis). Sarcomeres are laid down in parallel, thickening walls at the expense of chamber volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uniform, concentric thickening of the LV wall with a reduced cavity size is the hallmark of concentric hypertrophy, which arises when the ventricle must generate sustained high pressures against an increased afterload (hypertension, aortic stenosis). Sarcomeres are laid down in parallel, thickening walls at the expense of chamber volume.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal heart with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, highlighting obstructed outflow and mitral regurgitation. Which mechanism links septal hypertrophy to both of these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A ventricular septal defect shunting blood left-to-right

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve

explanation.whyCorrect: In obstructive HCM the hypertrophied septum plus high-velocity outflow draws the anterior mitral leaflet toward the septum (systolic anterior motion), simultaneously obstructing the outflow tract and creating mitral regurgitation.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: The diagram contrasts a normal ventricular cross-section with two remodeling patterns: one with a thick wall and small cavity, and one with a large cavity. Which stimulus produces the middle pattern (thick wall, reduced chamber volume)?

explanation.summary: Concentric hypertrophy (middle) results from pressure overload: increased systolic wall stress drives sarcomeres to be added in parallel, thickening the wall and reducing cavity volume. Eccentric hypertrophy (right, dilated) results instead from volume overload, with sarcomeres added in series.
explanation.whyCorrect: Concentric hypertrophy (middle) results from pressure overload: increased systolic wall stress drives sarcomeres to be added in parallel, thickening the wall and reducing cavity volume. Eccentric hypertrophy (right, dilated) results instead from volume overload, with sarcomeres added in series.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This figure shows a normal heart versus a thick-walled heart in which sarcomeres have been added in parallel within the myocytes. This structural change is the direct adaptive response to which condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sustained pressure overload of the ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sustained volume overload of the ventricle

explanation.summary: Adding sarcomeres in parallel widens each myocyte and thickens the ventricular wall, producing concentric hypertrophy. This is the response to pressure overload (high afterload). Adding sarcomeres in series (lengthening) produces eccentric hypertrophy in response to volume overload.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adding sarcomeres in parallel widens each myocyte and thickens the ventricular wall, producing concentric hypertrophy. This is the response to pressure overload (high afterload). Adding sarcomeres in series (lengthening) produces eccentric hypertrophy in response to volume overload.

questions.stem: This H&E-stained myocardial biopsy shows myocytes separated by expanded pale-staining fibrocollagenous tissue. This histologic pattern of interstitial infiltration/fibrosis stiffening the ventricular wall is the hallmark of which cardiomyopathy?

explanation.summary: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by increased ventricular wall stiffness from interstitial fibrosis or infiltration between myocytes, impairing diastolic filling while systolic function is often preserved.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restrictive cardiomyopathy is characterized by increased ventricular wall stiffness from interstitial fibrosis or infiltration between myocytes, impairing diastolic filling while systolic function is often preserved.

questions.stem: The left panel shows myocardium stained with a special dye, and the right panel shows the same field under polarized light where the deposits display apple-green birefringence. Which material is being demonstrated?

explanation.summary: Congo red stains amyloid, which shows pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light due to the beta-pleated sheet structure. This confirms cardiac amyloidosis as the cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congo red stains amyloid, which shows pathognomonic apple-green birefringence under polarized light due to the beta-pleated sheet structure. This confirms cardiac amyloidosis as the cause of restrictive cardiomyopathy.

questions.stem: This myocardial section is stained with a histochemical dye that turns intracellular deposits bright blue. In a patient with restrictive cardiomyopathy, diabetes, and bronze skin, what does the blue reaction identify?

explanation.summary: The Prussian blue (Perls) reaction stains ferric iron blue. Myocardial iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis or transfusional siderosis causes a restrictive/dilated cardiomyopathy; the triad of diabetes, skin pigmentation, and organ deposition is classic.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Prussian blue (Perls) reaction stains ferric iron blue. Myocardial iron overload in hereditary hemochromatosis or transfusional siderosis causes a restrictive/dilated cardiomyopathy; the triad of diabetes, skin pigmentation, and organ deposition is classic.

questions.stem: This cardiac imaging study (arrows indicating myocardial signal abnormality) is increasingly used to characterize infiltrative cardiomyopathies noninvasively, using late gadolinium enhancement and tissue mapping. Which modality is shown?

explanation.summary: Cardiac MRI provides tissue characterization; late gadolinium enhancement patterns and T1/T2 mapping help identify infiltrative and inflammatory causes of restrictive cardiomyopathy such as amyloid, sarcoid, and fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac MRI provides tissue characterization; late gadolinium enhancement patterns and T1/T2 mapping help identify infiltrative and inflammatory causes of restrictive cardiomyopathy such as amyloid, sarcoid, and fibrosis.

questions.stem: This H&E section of myocardium from a patient with restrictive physiology shows cardiomyocytes separated and surrounded by abundant pale, amorphous, acellular pink interstitial material. Which deposition process does this most likely represent?

explanation.summary: Cardiac amyloidosis deposits amorphous, eosinophilic, acellular protein in the interstitium and around myocytes, stiffening the ventricle and producing a restrictive cardiomyopathy with impaired diastolic filling.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac amyloidosis deposits amorphous, eosinophilic, acellular protein in the interstitium and around myocytes, stiffening the ventricle and producing a restrictive cardiomyopathy with impaired diastolic filling.

questions.stem: This myocardial biopsy shows a focal collection of epithelioid histiocytes and mixed inflammatory cells forming a granuloma surrounded by scarring, in a patient with heart block and restrictive physiology. Which infiltrative disease is most likely?

explanation.summary: Cardiac sarcoidosis produces noncaseating granulomas in the myocardium that can cause conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and a restrictive/infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes distinguishes it from bland fibrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac sarcoidosis produces noncaseating granulomas in the myocardium that can cause conduction blocks, arrhythmias, and a restrictive/infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Granulomatous inflammation with epithelioid histiocytes distinguishes it from bland fibrosis.

questions.stem: This gross four-chamber section of the heart shows markedly dilated left and right atria with non-dilated ventricles of relatively normal wall thickness. This atrial-predominant enlargement is the classic morphologic signature of which condition?

explanation.summary: Restrictive cardiomyopathy produces stiff ventricles with impaired diastolic filling; chronically elevated filling pressures dilate both atria while the ventricles remain normal in size. Marked biatrial enlargement with normal-sized ventricles is the hallmark gross finding.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restrictive cardiomyopathy produces stiff ventricles with impaired diastolic filling; chronically elevated filling pressures dilate both atria while the ventricles remain normal in size. Marked biatrial enlargement with normal-sized ventricles is the hallmark gross finding.

questions.stem: Comparing the two labeled diagrams of the heart, the abnormal one on the right has a stiffened ventricular wall with preserved chamber size. What is the primary hemodynamic consequence of this change?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduced systolic contractility with a dilated ventricle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impaired diastolic filling with preserved systolic function

explanation.summary: In restrictive cardiomyopathy the myocardium becomes stiff and non-compliant, limiting diastolic filling and raising filling pressures while ejection fraction is initially preserved. This causes biatrial enlargement and signs of right- and left-sided congestion.
explanation.whyCorrect: In restrictive cardiomyopathy the myocardium becomes stiff and non-compliant, limiting diastolic filling and raising filling pressures while ejection fraction is initially preserved. This causes biatrial enlargement and signs of right- and left-sided congestion.

questions.stem: This H&E section, magnified to show the junctional structures indicated, is taken from which tissue type?

explanation.summary: Intercalated discs are the step-like junctions unique to cardiac muscle; they contain desmosomes and gap junctions that mechanically and electrically couple cardiomyocytes. Desmosomal failure at these discs underlies ARVC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intercalated discs are the step-like junctions unique to cardiac muscle; they contain desmosomes and gap junctions that mechanically and electrically couple cardiomyocytes. Desmosomal failure at these discs underlies ARVC.

explanation.summary: The epsilon wave is a low-amplitude terminal deflection at the end of the QRS in V1, reflecting delayed activation of the fibrofatty-replaced right ventricular myocardium. It is a classic (though insensitive) ECG marker of ARVC.
explanation.whyCorrect: The epsilon wave is a low-amplitude terminal deflection at the end of the QRS in V1, reflecting delayed activation of the fibrofatty-replaced right ventricular myocardium. It is a classic (though insensitive) ECG marker of ARVC.

questions.stem: A 12-lead ECG shows a terminal QRS deflection in V1, T-wave inversion across V1-V3, and a prolonged S-wave upstroke. Taken together, these features point to which diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Epsilon waves, anterior precordial T-wave inversion (V1-V3), and prolonged terminal QRS/S-wave upstroke are the recognized ECG criteria for ARVC, all reflecting delayed right ventricular depolarization from fibrofatty replacement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Epsilon waves, anterior precordial T-wave inversion (V1-V3), and prolonged terminal QRS/S-wave upstroke are the recognized ECG criteria for ARVC, all reflecting delayed right ventricular depolarization from fibrofatty replacement.

explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac MRI in ARVC characteristically demonstrates RV free-wall thinning, fatty infiltration, dyskinesis/aneurysms, and RV dilatation, corresponding to fibrofatty myocardial replacement.

questions.stem: This H&E section of ventricular myocardium (arrows) shows residual pink muscle bundles separated by large pale spaces. What process does this represent in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coagulative necrosis of an acute infarct

explanation.summary: In ARVC, cardiomyocytes are progressively replaced by fat and fibrous tissue (the clear vacuolated areas are adipocytes). This creates a substrate for reentrant ventricular arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ARVC, cardiomyocytes are progressively replaced by fat and fibrous tissue (the clear vacuolated areas are adipocytes). This creates a substrate for reentrant ventricular arrhythmias and right ventricular dysfunction.

questions.stem: A patient with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy also has the thickened palmar and plantar skin shown here along with woolly hair. This inherited syndrome is known as?

explanation.summary: Naxos disease is a recessive desmosomal disorder combining ARVC with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair, reflecting the shared role of desmosomal proteins in cardiac myocytes and skin/hair.
explanation.whyCorrect: Naxos disease is a recessive desmosomal disorder combining ARVC with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair, reflecting the shared role of desmosomal proteins in cardiac myocytes and skin/hair.

questions.stem: This gross cross-section of the heart shows abundant yellow fatty tissue replacing the wall of one chamber (arrow). Which chamber is predominantly affected in the disease illustrated?

explanation.summary: In ARVC the right ventricular free wall is preferentially replaced by adipose and fibrous tissue, seen grossly as yellow fat thinning and infiltrating the RV wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: In ARVC the right ventricular free wall is preferentially replaced by adipose and fibrous tissue, seen grossly as yellow fat thinning and infiltrating the RV wall.

questions.stem: This gross heart specimen shows yellow adipose tissue replacing myocardium with residual thin trabeculations of the right ventricle. This fibrofatty replacement is the hallmark of which cardiomyopathy?

explanation.summary: Progressive replacement of RV myocardium by fat and fibrous tissue, leaving only thinned trabeculae, is the defining gross pathology of ARVC.
explanation.whyCorrect: Progressive replacement of RV myocardium by fat and fibrous tissue, leaving only thinned trabeculae, is the defining gross pathology of ARVC.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal heart with one affected by an inherited right ventricular cardiomyopathy. The abnormal tissue building up in the right ventricular wall most directly predisposes the patient to which complication?

explanation.summary: Replacement of RV myocardium by fibrofatty tissue disrupts electrical conduction and creates re-entry circuits, making malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (often in young athletes) the feared consequence of ARVC.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram of a young child shows a well-circumscribed intramural mass involving the ventricular myocardium. This tumor type is most strongly associated with which systemic condition?

explanation.summary: Cardiac rhabdomyomas are the most common cardiac tumor in children and are strongly linked to tuberous sclerosis (mutations in TSC1/TSC2). Many are detected prenatally or in infancy and frequently regress spontaneously.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac rhabdomyomas are the most common cardiac tumor in children and are strongly linked to tuberous sclerosis (mutations in TSC1/TSC2). Many are detected prenatally or in infancy and frequently regress spontaneously.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram shows a mobile, lobulated mass attached within a cardiac chamber, most often the left atrium near the interatrial septum. What is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Papillary fibroelastoma of the aortic valve

explanation.summary: Myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults, classically a gelatinous, pedunculated mass arising in the left atrium near the fossa ovalis; it can prolapse across the mitral valve and cause obstructive or embolic symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults, classically a gelatinous, pedunculated mass arising in the left atrium near the fossa ovalis; it can prolapse across the mitral valve and cause obstructive or embolic symptoms.

questions.stem: This gross specimen shows a heart sectioned to reveal a bulky, gelatinous, pale intracavitary mass filling an atrial chamber. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: The soft, gelatinous, myxoid appearance of a mass filling an atrial cavity is characteristic of myxoma, the most common primary cardiac tumor, which grows within the chamber and can obstruct valve inflow.
explanation.whyCorrect: The soft, gelatinous, myxoid appearance of a mass filling an atrial cavity is characteristic of myxoma, the most common primary cardiac tumor, which grows within the chamber and can obstruct valve inflow.

questions.stem: This H&E section of cardiac muscle shows enlarged cells with abundant clear, glycogen-filled vacuolated cytoplasm and thin cytoplasmic strands crossing the vacuoles (arrows). Which cardiac tumor does this histology represent?

explanation.summary: Rhabdomyoma, the most common primary cardiac tumor of children, is a hamartoma of cardiac myocytes. The tumor cells are large and vacuolated because glycogen is dissolved during processing, leaving strands of cytoplasm suspended across the clear space (the characteristic 'spider cell').
explanation.whyCorrect: Rhabdomyoma, the most common primary cardiac tumor of children, is a hamartoma of cardiac myocytes. The tumor cells are large and vacuolated because glycogen is dissolved during processing, leaving strands of cytoplasm suspended across the clear space (the characteristic 'spider cell').

questions.stem: This high-power H&E image shows a large cell with a central mass of eosinophilic cytoplasm and thin cytoplasmic processes radiating outward to the cell membrane across a clear space. This 'spider cell' is characteristic of which tumor?

explanation.summary: The 'spider cell' is pathognomonic of cardiac rhabdomyoma: glycogen is washed out during processing, leaving a large vacuolated cell whose residual cytoplasm forms strands stretching from a central nucleus-containing mass to the periphery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 'spider cell' is pathognomonic of cardiac rhabdomyoma: glycogen is washed out during processing, leaving a large vacuolated cell whose residual cytoplasm forms strands stretching from a central nucleus-containing mass to the periphery.

questions.stem: This diagram shows a pedunculated mass arising from the interatrial septum and projecting into the left atrium (magnified inset). What is this most common primary cardiac tumor of adults?

explanation.summary: Myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults, typically arising from the interatrial septum near the fossa ovalis in the left atrium. A pedunculated, mobile mass can obstruct the mitral valve ('ball-valve' effect) and embolize.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myxoma is the most common primary cardiac tumor in adults, typically arising from the interatrial septum near the fossa ovalis in the left atrium. A pedunculated, mobile mass can obstruct the mitral valve ('ball-valve' effect) and embolize.

questions.stem: This gross specimen of an opened heart shows a soft, pale, gelatinous mass attached by a stalk to the interatrial septum and protruding into the atrial chamber. What is this?

explanation.summary: Cardiac myxomas are typically soft, pale, gelatinous, pedunculated masses arising from the left atrial septum. Their friable surface predisposes to systemic embolization, and obstruction of the mitral valve can cause syncope or a 'tumor plop'.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cardiac myxomas are typically soft, pale, gelatinous, pedunculated masses arising from the left atrial septum. Their friable surface predisposes to systemic embolization, and obstruction of the mitral valve can cause syncope or a 'tumor plop'.

questions.stem: This H&E section shows scattered stellate and spindled cells (arrows), some forming small cords and rings, embedded in an abundant loose, pale myxoid (mucopolysaccharide-rich) stroma. Which cardiac tumor is this?

explanation.summary: Myxoma histology shows scattered stellate/lepidic myxoma cells, often arranged around vessels in rings and cords, set within a copious mucopolysaccharide (myxoid) matrix. The cells are thought to derive from primitive multipotent mesenchymal cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Myxoma histology shows scattered stellate/lepidic myxoma cells, often arranged around vessels in rings and cords, set within a copious mucopolysaccharide (myxoid) matrix. The cells are thought to derive from primitive multipotent mesenchymal cells.
